question: For the matrices $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&3&2\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$B=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&0\\-1&2\end{bmatrix},$$ calculate the product $AB$ and use the transpose of the relevant matrices to establish directly that $(AB)'=B'A'$.
explanation:
Evaluation of the Product

The order of $A$ is $2\times3$ and that of $B$ is $3\times2$, so $AB$ is defined and is of order $2\times2$. Thus, $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\0&3&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&0\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}1(2)+2(1)+(-1)(-1)&1(1)+2(0)+(-1)(2)\\0(2)+3(1)+2(-1)&0(1)+3(0)+2(2)\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}5&-1\\1&4\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$(AB)'=\begin{bmatrix}5&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification Using Transposes

We have $$B'=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&0&2\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$A'=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&3\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$B'A'=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&0&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&3\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}2(1)+1(2)+(-1)(-1)&2(0)+1(3)+(-1)(2)\\1(1)+0(2)+2(-1)&1(0)+0(3)+2(2)\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}5&1\\-1&4\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $(AB)'=B'A'$ for the given matrices.
